answer: A durable defence is a stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a refundable deposit, like copper set aside as collateral, before it can transact, and the deposit is slashed if peers attest fraud. New identities start with a narrow horizon of permissions and earn wider trust only through a basalt-solid record of completed, attested work over time. An attacker creating thousands of fake agents must fund every deposit and build every history, so the cost scales linearly with each Sybil while honest agents pay once.
